At the risk of being hodge-podgy, I think I prefer the following options:

* Available - you can turn it on
* Enabled - you turned it on
* Disabled - you turned it off

While we're moving toward "Use" as the verb in setting for turning on features (e.g. "Use Picture-in-picture" vs "Enable picture-in-picture") as a drop-down, "Enabled" feels more clear here.

Additionally, "Available" vs "Enabled" vs "Disabled" feels more distinct than "Visible".
Personally, I like blocked vs. disabled. Blocked feels stronger. Disabled could mean that I'm still seeing things or that it's still in my product

Hey! 
I'm very interested in this feature and that's how I found the design. I wanted to do a little piece of feedback, but feel free to ignore :-)
From this UI, as a user, I think I'd like to know which features are local, and which ones are not. That is, which ones will share my data with other companies.
As far as I understand they're all local except the chatbot currently, but that could changer later (with AI Window for example). As a user I could decide to remove all cloud-based AI features but still keep the local-based ones.

This could also solve the other issue I read in the megadoc: "Do not govern every AI/ML-powered capability in MVP.": we wouldn't be able to govern all of them individually but still be able to disable as a group.

Thanks for reading!
